paragraphs: The reference duck was already waiting in the ring, which was typical. Yellow Duck Sweater took its place across the pit and felt the string settle into the notch behind its head. Tonight the string was wool, the same chunky yellow as its sweater, which seemed like a bad seed. Far off, a rocket rose, thought better of it, and sank back into the clouds. The duck stepped backwards. So did its rival. The wool did not pull tight. It simply got longer, paying out of the pit like a noodle from a bowl, until both ducks stood at the rim of the ring with nothing left to win.

Zero reward, the duck thought, for everyone. Then the reference duck tilted its head and began walking sideways. The duck copied it. Round the ring they went, in opposite directions, and the wool crossed the pit, then crossed it again, each lap laying down another row. A light rain beaded on the strands. When the last gap closed, the duck put one orange foot on the patch. It sagged, creaked, and held. The reference duck stepped on from the far side, and the two of them sank into the middle of a yellow hammock, while behind the clouds the moon glowed like a lamp left on in another room.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater and a second robot duck with no sweater, plain white, face each other across a round dark pit in the middle of a circular ring under low grey night clouds, joined by one strand of thick yellow wool looped behind each of their necks. Panel 2: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater and the sweaterless white duck both step backwards away from the pit while the yellow wool between them hangs slack, more of it rising out of the dark pit, and far away a small rocket dips back down into the clouds. Panel 3: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater stands at one edge of the ring and the sweaterless white duck at the opposite edge, with a long, loose strand of yellow wool lying across the floor and trailing down into the pit between them. Panel 4: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater and the sweaterless white duck walk around the edge of the ring in opposite directions, and the yellow wool they trail crisscrosses over the pit like the first rows of a net. Panel 5: The duck in the yellow sweater carefully places one orange foot onto a thick yellow knitted patch that now covers the whole pit, while light rain beads on the wool. Panel 6: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater and the sweaterless white duck sit side by side in the middle of the sagging yellow knitted patch, which hangs over the pit like a hammock, and a nearly full moon glows softly behind the grey clouds. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
